titleEn: Small Business Renovation Vancouver 2026: What Metro Vancouver Businesses Actually Pay
titleZh: 溫哥華小企業裝修2026：大溫哥華地區商戶真實費用指南
contentEn:
Metro Vancouver small business owners spend between $20 and $500 or more per square foot on commercial tenant improvements — with most retail and office fit-outs landing in the $75–$200/sqft range. The wide spread reflects three choices that matter most: the condition of the existing space, the complexity of the work, and the municipality issuing the permit.

What Does a Small Business Renovation Actually Cost in Vancouver?

A small business renovation in Vancouver or Burnaby typically ranges from $20,000 for a basic retail refresh to $500,000 or more for a full change-of-use gut. Most projects Reno Stars handles for Metro Vancouver small businesses fall into three tiers.

Basic tenant improvements — new paint, flooring, upgraded lighting, and minor millwork — cost $20–$75 per square foot. A 1,000 sqft Vancouver coffee shop or boutique would budget $20,000–$75,000 for this scope.

Mid-range commercial fit-outs — custom cabinetry, upgraded washroom facilities, new partition walls, and integrated signage — cost $75–$200 per square foot. A 1,200 sqft Burnaby physiotherapy clinic or Langley physiotherapy clinic would budget $90,000–$240,000.

High-end or change-of-use builds — structural modifications, full mechanical and electrical upgrades, heritage building compliance — cost $200–$500 or more per square foot. A 2,000 sqft Port Moody restaurant or Richmond medical clinic in this range would budget $400,000–$1,000,000 or higher.

What Permits Does a Vancouver Small Business Renovation Need?

Every commercial renovation in Metro Vancouver requires a building permit. The permit type depends on your scope of work.

A tenant improvement permit — for work inside an existing commercial space that does not change the use or structure — is the most common for Vancouver, Burnaby, Surrey, and Richmond small businesses. Processing times range from 2 to 6 weeks depending on the municipality and the complexity of the submitted drawings. Permit fees follow a schedule tied to the estimated construction value, typically $500–$2,500 for standard retail or office fit-outs.

A change-of-use permit is required when a renovation changes the building's occupancy classification — for example, converting an old retail space into a restaurant or a warehouse into an office. This permit requires a registered professional to submit letters of assurance and often triggers additional requirements from the local fire authority and health authority for food-service uses. Processing times run 4 to 10 weeks.

Heritage commercial buildings in Vancouver's Gastown, Chinatown, and Strathcona districts require heritage review in addition to a standard building permit. Heritage alteration permits add 4 to 12 weeks to the timeline and typically carry a 20–40% cost premium due to required materials and finishes.

Every commercial renovation permit in British Columbia requires a $5M commercial general liability certificate from your contractor before the permit is issued. For restaurants, a health authority approval from Vancouver Coastal Health or Fraser Health is required in addition to the building permit — this process alone takes 2 to 4 weeks.

How Long Does a Small Business Renovation Take in Metro Vancouver?

Most small business renovations in Metro Vancouver complete in 4 to 16 weeks from permit submission to handover, with the fastest projects being basic tenant improvements and the longest being change-of-use builds in older buildings.

Permit processing by municipality varies significantly. Burnaby and Surrey typically process commercial permits in 2–4 weeks for standard tenant improvements. Vancouver's building department generally runs 3–6 weeks. New Westminster, Port Moody, and Coquitlam average 3–5 weeks. Langley and Maple Ridge process commercial permits separately from residential — expect 3–8 weeks for standard office or retail fit-outs. Heritage reviews in Vancouver add 4–12 weeks on top of the standard processing time.

Once permits issue, a basic retail fit-out (paint, flooring, millwork, signage) takes 3–6 weeks on site. A mid-range office or clinic fit-out with partition walls, upgraded washrooms, and mechanical work takes 6–10 weeks. A full change-of-use gut or restaurant renovation takes 10–16 weeks or longer on site.

Why Metro Vancouver Small Businesses Choose a Local Contractor

Vancouver's commercial renovation market runs on tight municipal rules. A Langley physiotherapy clinic needs different permit documentation than a Vancouver restaurant. A Burnaby dental clinic must meet Fraser Health infection control standards, while a Richmond retail boutique next to a food counter may require a food-adjacent occupancy review.

Reno Stars has managed commercial renovations across all Metro Vancouver municipalities — from a toy store fit-out in Metrotown, Burnaby to a skin lab transformation in Vancouver and a dental clinic renovation in Burnaby. Each project required different permit strategies, municipal coordination, and trades scheduling. That local knowledge directly affects how fast a small business opens its doors.

What is the average cost per square foot for a small business renovation in Vancouver?

Metro Vancouver small business renovations range $20–$75/sqft for basic tenant improvements, $75–$200/sqft for mid-range fit-outs, and $200–$500+/sqft for high-end or change-of-use builds. Most retail and office projects fall between $75 and $200 per square foot including materials and labour.

Does a Vancouver business renovation need a building permit?

Yes. Every commercial renovation in Vancouver, Burnaby, Surrey, Richmond, and across Metro Vancouver requires a building permit. Basic tenant improvements typically require a commercial tenant improvement permit. Changing the use of a space — for example, converting a retail unit into a restaurant — requires a change-of-use permit in addition to the building permit. Heritage buildings require a heritage alteration permit.

How long does a commercial renovation permit take in Metro Vancouver?

Permit processing times for commercial renovations vary by municipality. Burnaby and Surrey average 2–4 weeks. Vancouver and New Westminster run 3–6 weeks. Langley and Maple Ridge average 3–8 weeks. Change-of-use permits and heritage reviews add 4–12 weeks. Health authority approvals for food-service uses add 2–4 weeks on top of the building permit timeline.

Does a Vancouver contractor need insurance for commercial projects?

Yes. A $5M commercial general liability certificate from the contractor is required before any commercial building permit is issued in British Columbia. For restaurants, additional liquor liability and food-service-specific coverage may be required by the health authority. Reno Stars carries $5M commercial general liability for all projects in Metro Vancouver.

Can I renovate a heritage commercial building in Vancouver?

Yes, with additional requirements. Heritage commercial buildings in Vancouver's Gastown, Chinatown, and Strathcona districts require a heritage alteration permit in addition to a standard building permit. This adds 4–12 weeks to the approval timeline and typically increases costs by 20–40% due to required heritage-compliant materials and finishes. Reno Stars has managed heritage commercial renovation projects in Vancouver's historic districts.
